mission: Korea's AISI evaluates and researches AI safety and works with safety institutes in other countries. It says it is not a regulator: it aims to reduce risks that hurt Korean AI companies' competitiveness while protecting people. Under the AI Basic Act its tasks include defining AI risks, safety policy research, evaluation methods, safety technology and standards, and international cooperation.

key_work.title: South Korea's Approach to AI Governance: Mitigating Risks and Ensuring AI Safety
key_work.plain_summary: Director Kim Myuhng-joo explains the AI Basic Act, AISI's seven statutory functions and Korea's national AI risk map, which links each risk to the ministry responsible for responding.

key_work.title: AI Safety Research (institute research overview)
key_work.plain_summary: The institute's three offices: AI Safety Policy & External Cooperation, AI Safety Evaluation, and AI Safety Research Lab.

warnings.text: AI use creates risks to people's lives, physical well-being and property that need defining and tracking.
Risks span many ministries, so responsibility for responding can fall through the cracks without a shared risk map.

recommendations.text: Maintain a national AI risk map that assigns each risk to a responsible authority.
Develop AI safety evaluation criteria, methods and standards, and test jointly with partner institutes.
Support domestic AI firms to build safety in rather than relying only on regulation.
